static_traits.name: Zhou Li
static_traits.social_status: Relationship with friends is somewhat tense (often cancels plans with friends to prioritize fishing)
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no similar psychological problems before; no psychotherapy received yet
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly, cooperative positive attitude; can identify and describe own rigid thinking

basic_info.main_problem: Every weekend, if I can only fish one day and cannot go both days, I keep feeling disappointed and depressed, feeling the weekend is 'ruined', with dissatisfaction and a sense of missing out; worsened since a fishing trip was cancelled for work a few months ago.
basic_info.core_demands: These feelings of disappointment affect my overall mood and my enjoyment of weekends; I hope counseling can reduce the disappointment and increase the pleasure and flexibility of my weekends.

core_beliefs: Only by completing the weekend's two days of fishing as planned does my weekend have value
If the plan is disrupted, the whole experience equals failure

special_situations.event: On weekends, due to work arrangements or other matters, can only fish for one day
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot go fishing both days, this weekend is meaningless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Prioritizes fishing, squeezing or canceling other activities as much as possible to increase fishing time

special_situations.event: Having to cancel a planned fishing trip due to work commitments
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If plans are disrupted, it means this weekend is doomed to be unhappy
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries to rearrange my schedule and move other arrangements as much as possible to non-fishing times to maintain the rules
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This weekend will not be good, and it will be hard to enjoy in the future too

special_situations.event: Busy weekend schedule and other commitments reducing fishing time
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot devote the whole weekend to fishing, I will lose relaxation and enjoyment
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing plans with friends, arranging weekends more around fishing
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will definitely miss out on the most important enjoyment

special_situations.event: Friends proposing activities that conflict with fishing
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not choose fishing, it equals sacrificing the quality of the weekend
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Cancels activities with friends, prioritizing and securing the fishing arrangement
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Other activities are not worth it; I will still be unhappy

core_conflict.wish: Desiring to gain relaxation and satisfaction through stable, controllable weekend fishing
core_conflict.fear: Fears that after the plan is disrupted, the weekend loses meaning; feels intense disappointment and loss
defense_goal: Maintain rigid weekend rules to reduce anxiety
Prioritizes fishing and avoids other arrangements to secure a sense of control

object_relations.self_representation: Self that needs established rules in order to relax and feel satisfied
object_relations.object_representation: Friends (others) do not understand my needs; external commitments take away my happiness

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When a friend's invitation conflicts with fishing time, or work arrangements disrupt weekend plans
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Interpret any change as something that will 'ruin' weekend enjoyment (treating change as negative and unbearable)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Refusing others' invitations on the grounds of emphasizing the schedule and needing to relax, in a calm but firm tone, prioritizing ensuring the fishing plan.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When hearing others say 'do not understand why missing one day of fishing is so depressing'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believe others generally do not understand oneself and may look down on one's feelings (transference: projecting the feeling of not being understood onto others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizes others' attitudes and opinions, downplays exploration of their own rigid rules; uses defensive statements to protect existing arrangements.

manifestations: When unable to fish both days on the weekend, the experience is defined as 'ruined', 'not worth it'
Ties the meaning of the weekend solely to the single activity of fishing
outcomes: Losing motivation and interest in other activities

manifestations: Canceling plans with friends to prioritize fishing
Feel friends do not understand why one is so depressed
outcomes: Interpersonal tension and increased sense of alienation

manifestations: Bound by rigid weekend rules, hard to respond flexibly to changes
Treats 'must fish for two days' as a rigid standard
outcomes: Reduced choice flexibility, limited psychological flexibility
Weakened ability to adapt to change increases pressure

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Uses 'must fish two days', 'the weekend will otherwise be ruined' as rigid self-standards
Difficulty tolerating deviations and changes in plans

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Feel friends do not understand, and may even look down on one's feelings
Attributes the inner experience of being misunderstood to others' attitudes

positive_force: Holds a positive attitude toward counseling and is willing to practice reframing 'rules as wishes'
Has other interests (hiking, reading) that can serve as alternative activity resources
Work performance not yet affected, basic life stable
Able to identify own black-and-white and rigid thinking patterns
negative_force: Has rigid rules and black-and-white thinking about weekend activities
Overly tie weekend value to fishing, denying other positive experiences
Often cancel plans with friends to prioritize fishing, causing interpersonal tension
When plans are disrupted, tending to catastrophize and evaluate them as 'ruined'
Worry and fixation about missing out worsen disappointment and decreased drive

target_behavior.behavior: When weekend plans are disrupted, strong disappointment and frustration appear, repeatedly concluding 'the weekend is ruined'
antecedent: Work commitments or other matters preventing fishing on both days
Friends' activity invitations conflict with fishing time
target_behavior.core_reason: Holds a rigid all-or-nothing rule about the weekend experience, binding the weekend's meaning solely to fishing
target_behavior.function: Maintain a sense of control; avoid anxiety brought by uncertainty and change
target_behavior.consequence: Overall low mood, lack of motivation and interest in other activities, declining subjective weekend satisfaction

target_behavior.behavior: Frequently cancels plans with friends to prioritize fishing
antecedent: A friend's invitation conflicts with fishing plans
target_behavior.core_reason: Worries that missing fishing will lose the weekend's relaxation and satisfaction, regarding fishing as the only key activity
target_behavior.function: Gain more fishing time and sense of control; avoid discomfort from plan changes
target_behavior.consequence: Interpersonal tension, reduced social support, further worsening weekend dissatisfaction
